Reason: the keyboard acts where the person last acted, and a late programmatic focus that overrides a click reads as the app taking control (GTK and macOS return focus once, at close). Text ends at a grapheme-cluster boundary and trims punctuation per cluster, and DESIGN.md's "character boundary" says grapheme cluster. Reason: a cut inside a cluster draws a broken glyph (a lone combining mark, half a flag). Recorded in the briefs; the implementers write them into DESIGN.md / the crate docs.

      - Never type a full SHA by hand into a prompt or brief: paste it from `git rev-parse` (FU16-A's BASE carried an invented tail; the implementer recovered from the prefix).

      - A Linux-only caller (the Omarchy revision check) can leave a shared helper dead on macOS once another caller goes away: a reviewer's macOS cfg reading must include every caller of a function whose callers changed (FU15-A's `as_applied`).
      - A macOS-only layout failure reproduces on Linux by sweeping width and text size (and by swapping in macOS strings and temp paths): FU16-B matched the hosted failure string exactly.
      - An autosquash can conflict when a later fixup's hunk sits beside an earlier commit's edit of the same lines: keep that fixup as its own cohesive commit and check the tree equals the agent's tip.
      - A test oracle that reuses the product's own candidate set can pass vacuously: build it from what the frame shows (FU16-B review S1).

(3) FU14-B: centred controls keep their focus ring inside the row; one whose ring would reach the row above is lowered just enough; reason: a ring clipped by or overlapping the row above breaks whole focus. (4) FU14-E: the diagnostics allowlist holds only enumerated choices, booleans and numbers that change rendering (adds `reduce_motion` and `increase_contrast` stored and resolved, `follow_system`, `system_code_font`), never free text, paths, names, commands, branch names or pane widths; reason: the report is pasted into public issues. (2) A control taller than the view is revealed by its leading edge in both passes: the passes agree, so the scroll cannot swing, and the leading edge holds the label and first action. (3) A focus restore whose control is covered by Settings or a dialog leaves focus where it is and keeps the control as the covered page's return target: focus behind a modal is invisible and takes the next key. (4) Markdown images: declared dimensions refuse an image before decoding, the post-decode check stays as the backstop (a header can lie). - Known issues: a new macOS-only GPUI view-test flake most likely has one of #48's two causes: a reply from a real `SerialExecutor` thread that `run_until_parked` does not wait for (drain it with the test-only `SerialExecutor::drain()`), or a dialog's wall-clock animation (open it with reduced motion). Keep other builds off the host while a gate runs. The `gh` HTTPS token lacks the `workflow` scope, so a push that changes `.github/workflows/` is refused: push over SSH (`git push git@github.com:FernandoX7/GitTurtle.git <branch>`). In the agent-loop controller, a `blocked` status does not keep a task out of selection; hold a task by setting `attempts` to `max_attempts` and restore it later. A failed gate replaces the coordinator note and starts the next attempt at once. Background agents can hang on an `rm` with a glob, so delete with Python. Subagents cannot write report files, so they return findings as text, and a `SendMessage` to a busy background subagent is read only when its turn ends, so put every decision in the brief. Two traps from 2026-09-28 on the Pop!_OS host: another window took X focus during a QA run (17:02 to 17:05 UTC), so QA keys now go through the drivers' focus-checked sender; and two worktrees built into one `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` gave different commits an identical binary, so give each candidate its own target directory and check `--build-info`.
